name: ExplorerPatcher
description: Downloads ep_setup.exe and runs it ELEVATED (runas /update_silent), gated only by an 'MZ' magic-number + version check.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: ExplorerPatcher has a Windows application-update workflow. The retained review does not establish its complete artifact-authentication policy or the original impact classification.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study release; the cited code does not prove that MZ/version checks are the only gate or establish release artifact signing.

original_evidence.text: | ExplorerPatcher | github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher | Native C/C++ (DLL injected into `explorer.exe` + companion `ep_setup.exe`), GitHub-only distribution (no Store/winget) | Y — custom in-app/in-DLL updater (`ExplorerPatcher/updates.cpp`, `updates.h`) | Default policy is "notify" (`UPDATE_POLICY_DEFAULT UPDATE_POLICY_NOTIFY`, user-configurable to Auto/Notify/Manual via registry); the periodic check itself runs on a background thread (`CheckForUpdatesThread`) without user action | Y — on update, downloads `ep_setup.exe` (or staging asset) via WinInet to disk, then runs it with `ShellExecuteExW(lpVerb=L"runas", lpParameters=L"/update_silent")`, i.e. an elevated (UAC) silent install; if `UpdateUseLocal` is set it instead pipes a remote PowerShell script (`irm .../ep_make_safe.ps1 \| iex`) into `powershell.exe` | HTTPS via WinInet (`InternetOpenUrlW`/`InternetReadFile`) against `https://github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/releases/latest/download/<setup-name>` (stable) or `https://api.github.com/repos/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/releases?per_page=1` (staging, JSON-parsed for `browser_download_url`); default WinInet cert validation, no `INTERNET_FLAG_IGNORE_CERT_*` overrides found; the base update URL is itself read from a user/registry-writable `HKCU...UpdateURL` value, so any local process able to write that key can redirect updates | N (no manifest — direct binary download; the staging path parses raw GitHub API JSON, also unsigned) | none — the app reads only the first ~32 bytes of the incoming stream to (a) confirm an `MZ` (PE) header and (b) extract an embedded version string, comparing it to a locally computed value (`GetHardcodedHash`/`ComputeFileHash2`, itself just `fileVersion + MD5(local module)` used as a version fingerprint, not a manifest-supplied trust anchor); this is a version/sanity check, not a cryptographic integrity or authenticity check of the downloaded installer before it is executed with `runas` | n/a — no `WinVerifyTrust`/`CryptQueryObject`/Authenticode check exists anywhere in `updates.cpp`; whatever code-signing is on the actual EXE is never validated by ExplorerPatcher itself before execution | ExplorerPatcher/updates.h:35-37 (`UPDATES_RELEASE_INFO_URL_STABLE`, `UPDATES_RELEASE_INFO_URL_STAGING`); ExplorerPatcher/updates.cpp:369-393 (`InternetOpenUrlW` + `InternetReadFile` reading first bytes, `hash[0]==0x4D && hash[1]==0x5A` MZ check); :614-663 (download loop writing to `wszPath` via `InternetReadFile`/`fwrite`); :759-765 (`ShExecInfo.lpVerb = L"runas"`, `lpParameters = L"/update_silent"`, `ShellExecuteExW(&ShExecInfo)`); :925 (`szCheckAgainst` passed to `IsUpdateAvailableHelper`); ExplorerPatcher/utility.c:274 (`CryptCreateHash(hProv, CALG_MD5, ...)` — local-file version fingerprint, not payload verification), :329-347 (`ComputeFileHash2`, builds `"%d.%d.%d.%d." + MD5hex` string) |
